- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool.     description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

READ-ONLY audit. Do not edit, write, commit, or run anything that changes state.

Audit the skills in /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/ (each folder's SKILL.md plus any reference files it points to; skip _shared unless a skill points into it, skip .git, node_modules, caches, *-v1 backups only note they exist). Also note /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/CLAUDE.md.

Judge against these context-engineering principles (Anthropic, Claude 5 era). Judge the principle, not keywords:
2. Interfaces over examples: does a skill teach by boxing Claude into long worked examples / example transcripts where a clearer interface (parameters, names, structure, a script) would carry it?
4. One home over repetition: is the same instruction restated across several skills (or skill + CLAUDE.md), especially copies that have drifted apart? Check e.g. memory rules, git/commit rules, STATUS.md session routine, output-style rules, backup rules, closeout/startup/dev-sync/handoff overlap, design-taste-frontend vs design-taste-frontend-v1 vs impeccable, codex-build/codex-review/claudex-loop/claudex-route overlap.
6. Rich references over simple specs: do active build skills steer with prose descriptions where a higher-fidelity reference (runnable script, test, HTML mockup, rubric) exists or would be cheap?
1. Judgement over rules: absolute directives (MUST/NEVER/ALWAYS in caps) about taste or style, or directives that contradict each other. Do NOT flag safety, money, destructive-action, backup, approval, or health-data rules.
3. Also: skills whose frontmatter description is very long (over ~500 chars) — descriptions load into every session's skill listing. Measure full description length properly (multi-line YAML folded values count). Report top 10 by length with char counts.

Also check: are there skill folders in ~/.claude/skills that have `disable-model-invocation` or similar, and any skill whose description is missing/empty.

Return a compact report: for each principle, verdict PASS/FLAG, the 1-3 worst offenders with exact file path and a short quoted passage (under 25 words) that shows the problem, and a one-line suggested fix. Plus the description length top-10 table. Under 700 words. Cite only what you actually read.

##### ~/.claude/AGENTS.md
# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md`. Read that file first. On a new machine copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md`.

Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: the MacBook (`~/DEV`) and the Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`). Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive. Every project repo carries a Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` + read `docs/STATUS.md` at start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, `git push` at end.
# Workflow Expectations

- One home: the "Workflow Expectations" section of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read it there.

# graphify

- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) — turns any input into a knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`. When the user types `/graphify`, run that skill's workflow before doing anything else.

---

> **Why this file is not identical to `CLAUDE.md`.** Claude Code has a Skill tool, so `CLAUDE.md` routes memory work to the `memory-write` skill instead of restating it. Harnesses reading this file have no such tool, so the memory rules are spelled out below in full. The divergence is deliberate. **Do not symlink these two files together.** The canonical, most detailed copy is `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — if a rule below ever disagrees with that file, that file wins.

# Memory System

Two tiers.

## Tier A — per-project structured facts
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.

File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`.

**Slugs.** The slug is the cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-`:
`~` → `-Users-kristinarash` · `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`

**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows (Windows is active again as of 2026-09-10). Tier A written on one machine is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Prefer writing durable project facts to the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.

## Tier B — global working memory
`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).

Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.

## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. **Never write to them manually. Never read them eagerly** — treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## Session startup (silent — output nothing)

> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the
> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer
> states it. Codex has no equivalent hook, so the steps stay spelled out here.
> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.
Read in this order: `global-memory/USER.md`, then `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, then `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If `.errors.log` is non-empty, surface its contents once on the first response, then continue. It should normally be empty; entries indicate hook failures.

These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Never load more than this proactively.

## Writing — the steps
On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
2. Read the target file in full.
3. Dedup check (substring scan).
4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
6. Write.
7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

For **remove**: confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
Climb in order; stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — "I don't have a record of that."
##### DEV/AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md — ~/DEV workspace root

This repo tracks ONLY the workspace router files. It holds no project code.
Each project folder under `~/DEV` is its own git repo with its own remote.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## What lives here
`CLAUDE.md` is the workspace map. Read it first, then the one area index you need:
`FOOTBALL.md`, `PERFORMANCE.md`, `RESEARCH.md`, `PLATFORM.md`, `PROGRAM.md`,
`PERSONAL.md`, `COMMANDS.md`.

Note: `CLAUDE.md` here is NOT the usual one-line `@AGENTS.md` pointer. It is the
real workspace map and Claude Code loads it automatically. Leave it that way.

## Do not
- Do not `git add` a project folder. They are separate repos on purpose.
- Do not remove the `/*` rule in `.gitignore`. It is what keeps this repo thin.
##### skills/CLAUDE.md
# skills/CLAUDE.md

## MANDATORY: Use the CreateSkill skill for ALL skill work

Creating, modifying structure of, or validating any skill under this directory
REQUIRES invoking `Skill("CreateSkill")` first. Reading CreateSkill's workflows
and executing the steps by hand is NOT compliance — it is the exact
handrolling anti-pattern documented in feedback_invoke_blogging_skill_never_handroll.md.

### Triggers (MUST invoke CreateSkill)

- Creating a new skill directory
- Adding / removing / renaming Workflows, Tools, or References
- Editing SKILL.md frontmatter (name, description, effort, license)
- Validating an existing skill against canonical format
- Canonicalizing a legacy skill
- Public-clean audit

### NOT triggers (direct edits allowed)

- Fixing a typo in a single workflow file
- Updating the gotchas section in SKILL.md body (not frontmatter)
- Adding a new reference entry to an existing References/ file
- Accumulating lessons in an existing Gotchas section

### Enforcement

If you are about to `Write` or `Edit` a `SKILL.md`, a new file under
`Workflows/`, `Tools/`, or `References/`, or scaffold a new skill directory —
**STOP** and invoke `Skill("CreateSkill")` with your intent. Let the skill
orchestrate the work.

"I read CreateSkill's workflow and am now following its steps" is handrolling.
Invoke the skill; the skill invokes the steps.

# Memory System

Two tiers.

## Tier A — per-project structured facts
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.

File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`.

**Slugs.** The slug is the cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-`:
`~` → `-Users-kristinarash` · `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`

**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows (Windows is active again as of 2026-09-10). Tier A written on one machine is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Prefer writing durable project facts to the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.

## Tier B — global working memory
`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).

Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.

## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. **Never write to them manually. Never read them eagerly** — treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## Session startup (silent — output nothing)

> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the
> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer
> states it. Codex has no equivalent hook, so the steps stay spelled out here.
> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.
Read in this order: `global-memory/USER.md`, then `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, then `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If `.errors.log` is non-empty, surface its contents once on the first response, then continue. It should normally be empty; entries indicate hook failures.

These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Never load more than this proactively.

## Writing — the steps
On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
2. Read the target file in full.
3. Dedup check (substring scan).
4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
6. Write.
7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

For **remove**: confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
Climb in order; stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — "I don't have a record of that."

# AGENTS.md — ~/DEV workspace root

This repo tracks ONLY the workspace router files. It holds no project code.
Each project folder under `~/DEV` is its own git repo with its own remote.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## What lives here
`CLAUDE.md` is the workspace map. Read it first, then the one area index you need:
`FOOTBALL.md`, `PERFORMANCE.md`, `RESEARCH.md`, `PLATFORM.md`, `PROGRAM.md`,
`PERSONAL.md`, `COMMANDS.md`.

Note: `CLAUDE.md` here is NOT the usual one-line `@AGENTS.md` pointer. It is the
real workspace map and Claude Code loads it automatically. Leave it that way.

## Do not
- Do not `git add` a project folder. They are separate repos on purpose.
- Do not remove the `/*` rule in `.gitignore`. It is what keeps this repo thin.

# skills/CLAUDE.md

## MANDATORY: Use the CreateSkill skill for ALL skill work

Creating, modifying structure of, or validating any skill under this directory
REQUIRES invoking `Skill("CreateSkill")` first. Reading CreateSkill's workflows
and executing the steps by hand is NOT compliance — it is the exact
handrolling anti-pattern documented in feedback_invoke_blogging_skill_never_handroll.md.

### Triggers (MUST invoke CreateSkill)

- Creating a new skill directory
- Adding / removing / renaming Workflows, Tools, or References
- Editing SKILL.md frontmatter (name, description, effort, license)
- Validating an existing skill against canonical format
- Canonicalizing a legacy skill
- Public-clean audit

### NOT triggers (direct edits allowed)

- Fixing a typo in a single workflow file
- Updating the gotchas section in SKILL.md body (not frontmatter)
- Adding a new reference entry to an existing References/ file
- Accumulating lessons in an existing Gotchas section

### Enforcement

If you are about to `Write` or `Edit` a `SKILL.md`, a new file under
`Workflows/`, `Tools/`, or `References/`, or scaffold a new skill directory —
**STOP** and invoke `Skill("CreateSkill")` with your intent. Let the skill
orchestrate the work.

"I read CreateSkill's workflow and am now following its steps" is handrolling.
Invoke the skill; the skill invokes the steps.

---
name: skill-bloat-and-promotion
description: "Measured skill bloat in this setup, the project-until-promoted rule that fixes it, and the command that re-measures usage from .jsonl session logs"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f1097c6d-9db5-4bb5-a0f7-c42d645cf75d
  modified: 2026-09-13T06:38:22.028Z
---

Measured 2026-09-12 from a gap analysis of a Nate Herk / **Mark Kashef** video
("How to Actually Choose the Right AI Agent", 2026-09-11). Full note:
`~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-harness-over-model-mark-kashef.md`.
Same shape as the earlier audit in [[brain-audit-loop]] — that one scored the
**vault**, this one scores the **skill layer**.

## The measurement

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Global skills in `~/.claude/skills/` | 160 (→ **117** after the Tier 1 archive, 2026-09-12) |
| Plugin skills exposed per session | ~37 (6 enabled, 18 disabled) |
| SKILL.md files in plugin cache | 606 — disabled plugins + old versions, NOT the load |
| Project-level skills anywhere in `~/DEV` | **0** |
| `.jsonl` sessions scanned | 414 |
| Distinct real skills **ever** invoked | **58** |
| Used 3+ times | 30 |
| Used exactly once | 19 |

Everything is global. That is the anti-pattern, not the achievement.

## The rule that fixes it — promotion

**Everything stays project-level until it earns global.** A skill lives in
`<project>/.claude/skills/` until it proves itself across 2+ projects, then it
gets promoted to `~/.claude/skills/`. Keeps the global load small and the blast
radius tight — so when something underperforms you can tell a *model* problem
from a *harness* problem from an *organisation* problem.

## The audit question

Not "how often did I run this skill?" but **"would the model do this fine without
the skill now?"** A skill is a crutch; as the brain gets smarter the crutch starts
to *limit* it. Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`) and occasional ones
(`ingest-book`) are low-count by design — low usage alone is not a delete signal.

## Re-measure (BUILTIN filter is the whole trick)

Without the `BUILTIN` set you also count `/exit`, `/clear`, `/compact` and friends,
which inflates the total to 74 and buries the real skills.

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob,re,collections
BUILTIN={'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin','doctor',
'help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp','hooks','memory',
'review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir','bug','release-notes',
'pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline','output-style','todos','export',
'privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts','tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind',
'sandbox','feedback','worktrees','skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes',
'keybindings','theme'}
c=collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob('/Users/kristinarash/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl',recursive=True):
    try:
        for line in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'):
            if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
    except Exception: pass
real={k:v for k,v in c.items() if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}
print("distinct real skills ever invoked:",len(real))
print("used >=3 times:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v>=3]))
print("used exactly once:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v==1]))
for k,v in sorted(real.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1]): print(f"{v:5d}  {k}")
EOF
```

## Decision, 2026-09-12

**Do the skill audit BEFORE adopting Pi** (`pi.dev`) as an alternative harness.
Rationale: the leverage is the bloat, not the harness. Auditing first means any
future harness move ports ~30 good skills instead of ~200 mixed ones.

Pi facts, verified from `pi.dev/docs/latest` 2026-09-12 — full note at
`~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`:

1. **No sandbox, no approval flows.** "Pi does not include a built-in sandbox."
   Project trust only guards resource *loading*, not what the agent then does.
   Never run Pi in `~/DEV` or near `DexaProject`. Trial it in `~/pi-trial` or a
   container (`sbx` keeps the credential off the container).
2. **Skills port for one line.** Pi implements the Agent Skills standard and already
   auto-discovers `~/.agents/skills/` — where 45 of the skills live. Add the rest with
   `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]}` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. It loads
   `AGENTS.md` **or** `CLAUDE.md` directly.
3. **Hooks → TypeScript extensions is a bounded port, not a rewrite** (earlier note
   said "weeks", that was wrong). Hooks here are already `.ts`; Pi's `tool_call` event
   returns `{block, reason}` — the same shape as the dcg guard.
4. **Claude subscription through Pi bills per token as "extra usage", NOT against plan
   limits.** Changes the economics of brain-swapping.

Config lives in `~/.pi/agent/` and survives npm uninstall.
See also [[hook-two-copies-trap]] and [[dcg-guard-blocks]].

## Audit outcome, 2026-09-12

**Both tiers executed.** 99 skills archived, global **160 → 61**, roster cost
**19,158 → 6,428 tokens/session (a 66% cut)**. Zero regressions: none of the 99
had ever been invoked in 414 sessions.

Decision 2026-09-12: keep the `mattpocock-skills` and `superpowers` **plugins** and
archive the local bare-name duplicates. The plugin (v1.2.3, 35 skills) ships every
duplicate removed and is newer than the July symlinks. Rule that follows: when a
plugin and a local skill share a name, **the plugin wins** — delete the local copy.

Script: `~/.claude/skills-audit-2026-09-12.sh` (archives, never deletes — undo with
`mv ~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12/* ~/.claude/skills/`).
Report: `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-skill-audit.md`.

Traps found while doing it:
1. **CORRECTED 2026-09-12 — `~/.claude/skills/` IS version-controlled.** It is its own
   git repo, remote `https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git`, and the audit was
   committed as `3ab4467 chore: apply global skill audit` and pushed. The earlier note
   that it is "gitignored, archive is the only undo" was true only of the *`dotclaude`*
   repo, which ignores this path — a different thing. **Git IS the safety net here, and
   it is also how the cut reaches Windows.** Undo with
   `git -C ~/.claude/skills revert <sha> && git push`, not the archive folder
   (`skills-archive/` is not in the repo and never reaches the other machine).
2. **A cut in `~/.claude/skills/` does NOT reach `~/.agents/skills/`.** After the audit,
   98 of the 99 archived skills were still live in the pool (306 entries there vs 61
   canonical). Claude Code stopped seeing them; **Pi auto-discovers that folder**, so
   installing Pi would have re-exposed all of them. Always cut both.
3. **Skills live in three places and it is easy to edit the wrong copy.**
   `~/.claude/skills/` (19 entries were symlinks pointing *out* to the pool),
   `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork), `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex, 27 symlinks + 5 real

Not "how often did I run this skill?" but **"would the model do this fine without
the skill now?"** A skill is a crutch; as the brain gets smarter the crutch starts

(`ingest-book`) are low-count by design — low usage alone is not a delete signal.

1	# Machine
2	
3	Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md`. Read that file first. On a new machine copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md`.
4	
5	Two machines share this setup: the MacBook (`~/DEV`) and the Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`). Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive. Every project repo carries a Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` + read `docs/STATUS.md` at start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, `git push` at end.
6	# Workflow Expectations
7	
8	- One home: the "Workflow Expectations" section of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read it there.
9	
10	# graphify
11	
12	- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) — turns any input into a knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`. When the user types `/graphify`, run that skill's workflow before doing anything else.
13	
14	---
15	
16	> **Why this file is not identical to `CLAUDE.md`.** Claude Code has a Skill tool, so `CLAUDE.md` routes memory work to the `memory-write` skill instead of restating it. Harnesses reading this file have no such tool, so the memory rules are spelled out below in full. The divergence is deliberate. **Do not symlink these two files together.** The canonical, most detailed copy is `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — if a rule below ever disagrees with that file, that file wins.
17	
18	# Memory System
19	
20	Two tiers.
21	
22	## Tier A — per-project structured facts
23	`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.
24	
25	File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`.
26	
27	**Slugs.** The slug is the cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-`:
28	`~` → `-Users-kristinarash` · `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`
29	
30	**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows. Tier A written on one machine is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Prefer writing durable project facts to the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
31	
32	## Tier B — global working memory
33	`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
34	- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
35	- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
36	- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).
37	
38	Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.
39	
40	## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
41	`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. **Never write to them manually. Never read them eagerly** — treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.
42	
43	## Session startup (silent — output nothing)
44	
45	> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the
46	> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer
47	> states it. Codex has no equivalent hook, so the steps stay spelled out here.
48	> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.
49	Read in this order: `global-memory/USER.md`, then `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, then `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If `.errors.log` is non-empty, surface its contents once on the first response, then continue. It should normally be empty; entries indicate hook failures.
50	
51	These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Never load more than this proactively.
52	
53	## Writing — the steps
54	On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
55	1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
56	2. Read the target file in full.
57	3. Dedup check (substring scan).
58	4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
59	5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
60	6. Write.
61	7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`
62	
63	For **remove**: confirm with the user before deleting.
64	
65	## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
66	Climb in order; stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.
67	
68	1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
69	2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths.
70	3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
71	4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
72	5. **Fallback** — "I don't have a record of that."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Block commits when CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md diverge.
# AGENTS.md must be a byte-identical mirror of CLAUDE.md so any agent
# (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) reads the same project memory.
#
# Activate once per clone: git config core.hooksPath .githooks
# If you intentionally need to diverge, update this hook first.

set -e

if [ ! -f CLAUDE.md ] || [ ! -f AGENTS.md ]; then
    # If either is missing on this commit, let it through — covers the initial
    # commit and deliberate removal. Other tooling (or CI) can enforce presence.
    exit 0
fi

if ! cmp -s CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md; then
    echo "ERROR: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md have diverged." >&2
    echo "       Run:  cp CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md  &&  git add CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md" >&2
    echo "       Or update .githooks/pre-commit if divergence is intentional." >&2
    exit 1
fi

exit 0
.githooks

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

# PFF Data Project — Agent Guide

This file is the canonical project memory for any AI coding agent working in this
repo. It is mirrored verbatim into `AGENTS.md` so OpenAI Codex (and any other
agent that reads `AGENTS.md`) gets the same context. A pre-commit hook in
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits where the two files diverge.

If you edit one, edit both. See "Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync" below.

---

## What this project is

A standalone Python data pipeline that pulls Pro Football Focus (PFF) game and
player data into a local **DuckDB** database for Baylor University Football
analysis. Scope is **Baylor + every Big 12 team + non-conference opponents** for
the **current season plus two prior**.

The DB *is* the deliverable. There are no dashboards in this repo. Downstream
consumers — Power BI, Jupyter notebooks, and a future athlete management system
(AMS) project that will unify PFF with Catapult GPS, VALD ForceDecks, and Perch
VBT data — own visualization and cross-domain joins.

## Sister pipelines (do not modify from here)

- **VALD ForceDecks (CMJ/IMTP):** `..\..\ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` — the
  architectural template this project mirrors.
- **Catapult GPS:** `..\..\DataBase_GPS_Reporting`
- **Perch VBT:** not yet built.

The pattern across all of them is: per-domain Python pipeline → per-domain DB →
future AMS layer unions them on `(athlete_id, source_system, pulled_at)`.

## Tech stack

- Python 3.12+
- `duckdb`, `requests`, `python-dotenv`, `PyJWT`, `pyyaml`, `pandas`, `pytest`
- No web framework, no ORM, no dashboard libs — keep it lean

## Layout

```
PFF_Data_Project/
├── CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md       # this file (mirrored)
├── README.md                   # user-facing setup and usage
├── requirements.txt
├── .env.example                # PFF_BASE_URL, PFF_API_KEY, BAYLOR_TEAM_ID
├── .gitignore
├── .githooks/pre-commit        # blocks CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md divergence
├── run_pipeline.py             # CLI entry
├── config/
│   └── pipeline.yaml           # team/season scope, endpoints, retry config
├── src/
│   ├── db.py                   # DuckDB schema + connect + backup helpers
│   ├── ingest/
│   │   ├── pff_client.py       # PFF HTTP client (stub until Phase 0 done)
│   │   └── pipeline.py         # Orchestration: dims → facts → log
│   └── shape/transform.py      # JSON → tidy rows (teams/games/grades/stats/premium)
├── data/                       # DuckDB lives here (gitignored)
├── docs/
│   └── pff_api_notes.md        # Phase 0 spike output
├── scripts/
│   └── phase0_probe.py         # Credential discovery probe
└── tests/
    ├── test_db.py
    └── fixtures/
```

## Data model contract

Dimensions are stable identities; facts are timestamped measurements.

- **Dimensions:** `teams`, `players`, `player_seasons`, `games`
- **Facts:** `pff_grades` (per-player per-game, long form), `pff_stats` (extended
  stats, long form), `pff_premium` (advanced metrics, keyed JSON passthrough)
- **Operational:** `ingest_log`

`players` / `player_seasons` are derived from the grade rows (which carry
player_id, name, position, team_id, season) — cleanest "who actually played"
source; avoids the giant all-NCAA `/players` pull.

Every fact row carries `source_system = 'PFF'` and `pulled_at`. This is
non-negotiable — it is the contract the future AMS layer relies on to union PFF
with Catapult, VALD, and Perch facts.

`pff_player_id` is the durable join key. This pipeline does **not** maintain a
canonical athlete master record across systems. That mapping
(`roster.athlete_id → pff_player_id`) belongs to the future AMS project. Do not
invent it here.

## API contract (Phase 0 complete)

Full contract is in `docs/pff_api_notes.md`; OpenAPI specs in `docs/swagger/`.
Essentials:

- **Auth:** `POST /auth/login` with header `x-api-key: <key>` → `{"jwt"}`. Send
  `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on all calls. JWT lasts ~1h; re-auth on 401.
  Rate-limited (HTTP 429) — client backs off. `src/ingest/pff_client.py` owns this.
- **Base:** `https://api.profootballfocus.com`, league slug `ncaa`, season = year.
- **Baylor:** team_id / franchise_id = `118` (`BAYLOR_TEAM_ID` in `.env`).
- **Scope is open:** the key reads all NCAA teams + grades for any game, so
  Baylor + Big 12 + opponents is achievable despite the token's `franchise:118`
  constraint.
- **Play-by-play exists in the Video Feeds API** (EPA fields confirmed 2026-09-13):
  `/v1/video/ncaa/games/{game_id}/plays`, 330+ fields per play, including PFF EPA
  (`expected_points_added` and `expected_points_added_legacy`). Ingested for Baylor
  2024-2025 into `pff_premium` as category `video_plays` by
  `scripts/pull_video_plays.py`; deliberately not in `PREMIUM_CATEGORIES` (the
  season loop would pull every scoped game at ~1.5 MB each).
- **Full seasons stream from `/v1/video/ncaa/{season}/plays`** (~2.5 GB decoded,
  about a minute): `scripts/pull_season_video_plays.py --season YYYY` writes
  `data/video_plays_slim_<season>.parquet` (31 fields per play) and
  `data/video_games_<season>.parquet` (final scores; the plays feed only has the
  score before each snap). Both gitignored. `season_plays.to_frame` must build
  the frame with `dtype=object`: without it an int column with a gap becomes
  float64 and is stored as the text `"2.0"` and `"nan"`.
  Premium feeds (`/v1/premium/...`) provide play-level advanced metrics → captured
  in `pff_premium` as keyed JSON passthrough. All 12 API specs are in `docs/swagger/`.
- **FUTURE:** player-tracking feeds are deliberately not modeled in v1.

## Conventions

- **Credentials never in code.** `.env` only. Loaded via `python-dotenv`. The
  `.env` file is gitignored; `.env.example` is committed as the template.
- **DuckDB upserts:** use `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO` (idempotent refresh — re-pulling
  a week updates values rather than duplicating). See `_upsert` in `pipeline.py`.
- **Config path resolution:** always anchor to `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`
  walks, never relative paths from CWD. `run_pipeline.py` and `src/db.py` show
  the pattern.
- **Backups before destructive ops:** copy `data/pff.db` to
  `data/pff_before_<operation>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.db` first.
  `src/db.backup_db()` does this — use it from any new destructive code path.
- **Idempotent ingests:** running the same week twice must be a no-op.
- **One concern per module.** Client does HTTP. Shape does JSON-to-rows. Pipeline
  orchestrates. db.py owns the schema. Don't blur these.
- **Tests use mocked HTTP**, not live API calls. The Phase 0 probe is the only
  script that hits the real API.
- **No comments that narrate the obvious.** Comments are for non-obvious WHYs
  (e.g., "DuckDB requires ON CONFLICT here; SQLite syntax silently fails").

## CLI commands

```
python run_pipeline.py --dry-run               # auth + scope check, no writes
python run_pipeline.py --backfill              # full 3-season pull
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025           # full season
python run_pipeline.py --season 2025 --week 8  # one week
python run_pipeline.py --diagnose [NAME]       # query local DB
python run_pipeline.py --reset-db              # backup + reinit
```

## Testing

```
pytest tests/
```

Tests that need a DB use a per-test temp path; don't touch `data/pff.db`.

## Keeping CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync

`AGENTS.md` is a byte-identical copy of `CLAUDE.md`. The pre-commit hook at
`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks commits when they differ. Activate the hook once
per clone:

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

When updating agent guidance, edit `CLAUDE.md` first, then:

```
cp CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
git add CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
```

If you intentionally need them to diverge (tool-specific instructions for one
agent), update the hook before committing — don't bypass it silently with
`--no-verify`.

## Working with this repo from Codex

Codex reads `AGENTS.md` automatically. Everything above applies to Codex
sessions identically. Codex-specific notes, if any are ever needed, go in a
separate section here and get mirrored.


## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

c=collections.Counter(); sessions=0
for f in glob.glob(os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl'),recursive=True):
    sessions+=1
    try:
        for line in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'):
            if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line and 'ctx_' not in line: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line): c['model:'+m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line): c['typed:'+m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__(ctx_\w+)"', line): c['mcp:'+m.group(1)]+=1
    except Exception: pass
print("sessions",sessions)
pref=('superpowers','context-mode','ctx','mattpocock','codex','last30days','watch','brainstorm','systematic','test-driven','writing-plans','executing-plans','verification','dispatching','subagent-driven','using-git','finishing','requesting','receiving','writing-skills','grill','tdd','prototype','diagnos','research','domain','codebase','code-review','resolving','wizard','handoff','zoom','caveman')

EOF
